claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To do this properly, I'll need to ask you some questions about your circumstances and your child or children.

Let me start with the first question:

**How many children are you looking to claim Child Benefit for, and what are their names and ages?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I'm wondering about claiming Child Benefit. I have one child - my son Alex, he's 17.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. Since Alex is 17, there are some specific rules that apply. Let me ask you the next question:

**Is Alex currently in approved education or training?** For example, is he at school, college, university, or doing an approved apprenticeship or training course?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not in any education or training at the moment. He finished school and decided not to continue with his studies.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. Since Alex has left education or training, I need to ask:

**Has Alex registered with either a government-sponsored careers service or the armed services since leaving education?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he hasn't registered with a careers service or the armed forces. He just left school and has been working.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. Now I need to ask about his work:

**How many hours per week is Alex working, and is he getting any benefits in his own right (such as Employment and Support Allowance or Universal Credit)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He's working full-time - it's at least 24 hours a week. And no, he doesn't get any benefits in his own name.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I appreciate you providing that information. Let me also confirm one more important detail:

**Are you living in the UK, and do you live with Alex?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK and Alex lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for all that information. I now have enough details to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

Based on the rules provided, I can see that you would **not be eligible** for Child Benefit for Alex. Here's why:

According to the Child Benefit rules, you stop getting Child Benefit when your child starts paid work for 24 hours or more a week **and is no longer in approved education or training**. 

In Alex's case:
- He is working full-time (24+ hours per week)
- He is no longer in approved education or training
- He has not registered with a careers service or the armed forces (which would allow a 20-week continuation period)

Since both of these conditions are met, Child Benefit eligibility ends.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I'm afraid you're not eligible for Child Benefit for Alex at this time. However, if circumstances change - for example, if Alex were to leave work and register with a careers service or the armed forces - the situation could be different, as there would be a 20-week continuation period available. If you'd like more information or if your circumstances do change, you can contact the Child Benefit Office for further guidance.
